profile.reading:
CloudHQ MCC1 sits at 10880 Airman Avenue, Manassas, Virginia, part of CloudHQ's MCC Campus, which the company's own current campus page describes as "CloudHQ's original campus location," on the south side of Manassas in Prince William County, connected to CloudHQ's adjacent "MDC campus" and to regional fiber via the "Manassas Fiber Highway." Trade press reported MCC1's original 2017 opening at 460,000 square feet and 43 megawatts, a dated historical figure this profile notes as not necessarily reflecting the building's current capacity. CloudHQ states the full MCC Campus totals 2,232,875 square feet and 382 megawatts of total critical IT load across seven data centers, with 96 megawatts currently available, describing MCC5 as site-plan approved and ready for immediate development and MCC7's construction as beginning mid-2025 with an expected Q3 2026 ready-for-service date; CloudHQ's current site does not individually disclose MCC1's present-day capacity, so the campus total is not applied to this specific building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust, and is privately held through the Fateh Family Office. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the MCC Campus on its current site; Prince William County's data center corridor is served by a mix of Dominion Energy and NOVEC (Northern Virginia Electric Cooperative) territory depending on specific location, and this profile does not assert which utility serves MCC1 specifically without independent confirmation.

Prince William County's Manassas-area data center corridor has grown alongside Loudoun County's much larger Ashburn cluster, though the two submarkets have followed somewhat different zoning and community-engagement trajectories; Prince William County has seen significant public debate in recent years over large-scale data center rezoning proposals near residential areas and historic sites, though this profile does not confirm CloudHQ's MCC Campus specifically as a party to any particular zoning controversy without independent sourcing. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide.

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC1 publishes one hard number: 2,232,875 square feet of technical space in Prince William County, Virginia. That figure places the campus among the largest footprints in a state already dense with data center infrastructure. No IT load in megawatts, no critical power figure, and no redundancy tier are published on the operator's spec page, so no power-based estimate of rack or accelerator capacity can be responsibly made here.

Without a published megawatt figure, this site cannot rank MCC1 among the 19 Virginia facilities that do publish capacity. Those 19 facilities together account for 1,326 MW of published IT load across the state, and MCC1 is not among them. Whether its actual power draw is large or small relative to that pool is not determinable from what the operator has released.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, the square footage signals that the physical shell exists at scale, but shell space alone does not confirm power delivery, cooling infrastructure, or network density, all of which determine whether a building can support high-density GPU training or inference workloads. No certifications are listed in the published specifications. Until CloudHQ publishes a critical IT load figure, MCC1 remains a large building whose AI hosting capacity is unknown.
